Below is a concise “long‑weekend” calendar for Canada in **2023**.  
It lists the *national* holidays that create an extended weekend (i.e., the holiday falls on a weekday or is observed on a Monday when it lands on a weekend).  
For each entry you’ll see:

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Span |
|---------|-------------|-------------|-------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 | Sunday | **Jan 1–3** (holiday on Sunday + weekend) |
| Family Day (Ontario, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island) | Feb 20 | Monday | **Feb 18–20** |
| Family Day (British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Newfoundland & Labrador, Yukon, Northwest Territories, Nunavut) | Mar 20 | Monday | **Mar 18–20** |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 | Friday | **Apr 7–9** (Fri‑Sun) |
| Victoria Day | May 22 | Monday | **May 20–22** |
| Canada Day (observed) | Jul 3 | Monday | **Jul 1–3** (holiday on Sat → observed Mon) |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 | Monday | **Sep 2–4** |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 | Monday | **Oct 7–9** |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 | Monday | **Nov 9–11** |
| Christmas Day | Dec 25 | Monday | **Dec 23–25** |
| Boxing Day | Dec 26 | Tuesday | **Dec 23–26** (extended holiday) |

### How to use this in your app

1. **Filter by Province** – If you need province‑specific holidays (e.g., Family Day dates differ), add a filter that selects the appropriate dates above.  
2. **Highlight Long‑Weekends** – Use the “Long‑Weekend Span” column to color‑code or flag these periods in your UI.  
3. **Calendar Integration** – When generating a calendar view, mark the holiday dates and automatically extend the weekend block to include the adjacent weekend days.  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the same list broken down by province or if you need additional holidays (e.g., provincial holidays that aren’t national).
